question: 'She has been reading since morning' — kaun sa tense hai?
option_e: Unattempted — mark E only if deliberately leaving this question blank
explanation: Sahi: B — 'Has been reading' + 'since morning' = Present Perfect Continuous (has/have been + V-ing; kaam subah se ab tak chal raha hai). | Galat kyun: Present Perfect hota to 'has read' hota; Past Continuous hota to 'was reading' hota; Future Perfect hota to 'will have read' hota. | Concept: Tense pehchan — helping verb + verb form. | Yaad rakhne ke liye: has been + -ing = Perfect Continuous; 'since' ke saath aksar yahi tense aata hai. | Source: notes/13_general_english.md §13.1.

question: 'Ram writes a letter' ka passive kya hai?
option_a: A letter is wrote by Ram
option_b: A letter has written by Ram
option_c: A letter was written by Ram
option_d: A letter is written by Ram
option_e: Unattempted — mark E only if deliberately leaving this question blank
explanation: Sahi: D — Present Simple passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 → 'A letter is written by Ram.' | Galat kyun: 'is wrote' galat hai (V3 'written' chahiye, V2 nahi); 'has written' active perfect hai (passive nahi); 'was written' past ka passive hai (present nahi). | Concept: Active → Passive — be + past participle (V3). | Yaad rakhne ke liye: Passive me hamesha V3 (written, eaten) aata hai. | Source: notes/13_general_english.md §13.2.

question: 'He said, I am busy' ka indirect kya hai?
option_a: He said that he is busy
option_b: He said that he has been busy
option_c: He said that he will be busy
option_d: He said that he was busy
option_e: Unattempted — mark E only if deliberately leaving this question blank
explanation: Sahi: D — Direct se Indirect me reporting verb past ('said') ho to andar ka Present Simple Past Simple me badalta hai: 'I am busy' → 'he was busy'. | Galat kyun: 'is busy' (tense nahi badla), 'has been busy' (perfect — galat badlav) aur 'will be busy' (future — galat) teeno galat hain. | Concept: Direct → Indirect — tense ek kadam peeche jata hai (Present → Past). | Yaad rakhne ke liye: said + present → was (past). | Source: notes/13_general_english.md §13.2.

question: 'He has been ill ___ Monday' — sahi preposition?
option_e: Unattempted — mark E only if deliberately leaving this question blank
explanation: Sahi: A — 'Since' = samay ka bindu (point of time — Monday, 2020, morning); 'He has been ill since Monday' — bimaari Monday se shuru hui. | Galat kyun: 'For' avadhi (duration — three days) ke liye hota hai; 'by' aur 'from' yahan sahi nahi hain ('from' ke saath present perfect continuous nahi banta). | Concept: Since = point of time; For = duration. | Yaad rakhne ke liye: Since + Monday (ek din), For + three days (avadhi). | Source: notes/13_general_english.md §13.4.

question: 'She ate an apple' ka passive kya hai?
option_a: An apple has eaten by her

question: Passage: 'The camel is called the ship of the desert. It can walk for many days in the hot desert without water. It carries people and heavy loads across the sand.' — Camel ko 'ship of the desert' kyun kaha jata hai?
option_a: It carries people and loads across the desert
option_b: It can live without water for many days
option_c: It is the fastest animal in the desert
option_e: Unattempted — mark E only if deliberately leaving this question blank
explanation: Sahi: A — Passage ke anusar camel desert me logon aur bojh ko le jata hai — jaise jahaz samudra me logon aur saaman ko le jata hai; yahi 'ship' wali tulna hai, isliye 'ship of the desert'. | Galat kyun: B (bina pani ke kai din reh sakta hai) passage me sahi hai, lekin yah 'ship' tulna ko nahi samjhata — jahaz ki tulna bojh le jane se hai, pani ke bina rehne se nahi; C (sabse tez) passage me nahi kaha gaya; D (sirf Rajasthan) galat hai — camel kai deserts me milta hai. | Concept: Comprehension — prashn ka uttar passage ki tulna (comparison) se milta hai, sirf sahi tathya se nahi. | Yaad rakhne ke liye: Ship = le jane wala (carry) — camel desert ka jahaz hai kyunki vah bojh le jata hai. | Source: notes/13_general_english.md §13.5 (passage ke aadhar par).
